at lade.explanation: "At lade" means "to let", as in allowing: Hun lader ham gå (She lets him go). It can also mean "to leave something as it is": Jeg lader nøglen ligge (I leave the key lying there).

sentence.da: Mor vil ikke **lade** os gå alene.
sentence.en: Mom won't let us go alone.

at lade som om.explanation: "At lade som om" means "to pretend". What you pretend comes after it as a full sentence: Han lader som om han sover (He pretends he is sleeping).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lade som om** de er pirater.
sentence.en: The children want to pretend they are pirates.

at lade være.explanation: "At lade være" means "to not do" something: Lad være med at råbe! (Don't shout!). Add med at and the action: Jeg lader være med at ryge (I refrain from smoking). Alone, Lad være! means "Don't!".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lade være** med at spise slik.
sentence.en: I will refrain from eating candy.

at lande.explanation: "At lande" means "to land", mostly for planes: Vi lander i København klokken tre (We land in Copenhagen at three). It also works for a bird: Fuglen landede i træet (The bird landed in the tree).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lande** om en time.
sentence.en: The plane will land in an hour.

at larme.explanation: "At larme" means "to make noise", usually more than others would like: Naboen larmer (The neighbor is making noise).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **larme** efter klokken ti.
sentence.en: The children must not make noise after ten o'clock.

at lave.explanation: "At lave" means "to make" or "to do": Hvad laver du? (What are you doing?) and Jeg laver en kage (I am making a cake).

forms.en: I have made, I have done

sentence.da: Hvad skal vi **lave** i aften?
sentence.en: What are we going to do tonight?

at lave en fejl.explanation: "At lave en fejl" means "to make a mistake": Jeg lavede en fejl i regnestykket (I made a mistake in the math problem). With more than one, drop en: Alle laver fejl (Everyone makes mistakes).

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **lave en fejl**.
sentence.en: I am afraid of making a mistake.

at lave lektier.explanation: "At lave lektier" means "to do homework". Danish says lave (to make) where English says "do": Har du lavet dine lektier? (Have you done your homework?).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **lave lektier** nu.
sentence.en: The children have to do homework now.

at lave mad.explanation: "At lave mad" means "to cook". It is made of lave (to make) and mad (food), so it literally means "to make food". Add the dish when you say what you cook: Jeg laver pasta (I am making pasta).

sentence.da: Min far vil **lave mad** i aften.
sentence.en: My father will cook tonight.

at lave om.explanation: "At lave om" means "to change" or "to redo" something you already made: Jeg laver opgaven om (I am redoing the assignment). To change part of something, add på: Jeg laver om på planen (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Hun skal **lave om** på hele rapporten.
sentence.en: She has to change the whole report.

at lave sjov.explanation: "At lave sjov" means "to joke around": Han laver sjov hele dagen (He jokes around all day). To tease someone, add med: Hun laver sjov med mig (She is teasing me).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **lave sjov**, og alle griner.
sentence.en: My brother loves to joke around, and everyone laughs.

at le.explanation: "At le" means "to laugh": Hun ler højt (She laughs out loud) and Vi lo meget (We laughed a lot). To laugh at someone, add af: Han ler af mig (He is laughing at me).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **le** af den sjove film.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny film.

at lede.explanation: "At lede" means "to lead", and with efter (for) it means "to search": Hun leder holdet (She leads the team). Jeg leder efter mine nøgler (I'm looking for my keys).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **lede** efter min hat.
sentence.en: I have to look for my hat.

at lede efter.explanation: "At lede efter" means "to look for" something you cannot find yet: Jeg leder efter min taske means "I am looking for my bag". Do not mix it up with at se på (to look at), which is for something you can already see.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lede efter** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I want to look for my keys.

at lege.explanation: "At lege" means "to play" the way children do, just for fun: Børnene leger i haven (The children are playing in the garden). For sports, games and instruments Danish uses at spille (to play).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lege** med bolden i haven.
sentence.en: The children want to play with the ball in the garden.

at leje.explanation: "At leje" means "to rent", when you pay to use something: Vi lejer en bil (We are renting a car). For the owner who rents it out, use at udleje (to rent out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **leje** en bil i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to rent a car for the weekend.

at lette.explanation: "At lette" means "to take off", for a plane: Flyet letter fra Kastrup (The plane takes off from Kastrup). It can also mean "to make easier": Det letter arbejdet (That makes the work easier).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lette** om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The plane takes off in five minutes.

at leve.explanation: "At leve" means "to live (be alive)": Hun lever stadig (She is still alive). It is also used for how you live your life: leve et godt liv (to live a good life). For where your home is, Danes say at bo (to live somewhere).

sentence.da: Fisk kan ikke **leve** uden vand.
sentence.en: Fish cannot live without water.

at lide.explanation: "At lide" means "to suffer", usually with af: Han lider af hovedpine (He suffers from headaches). Do not mix it up with kan lide (like): Jeg kan lide kaffe (I like coffee).

sentence.da: Dyrene vil **lide**, når der ikke er mere vand.
sentence.en: The animals will suffer when there is no more water.

at ligge.explanation: "At ligge" means "to lie (be lying)", to be lying down or placed flat: Bogen ligger på bordet (The book is lying on the table). It also says where places are: Byen ligger ved havet (The town is by the sea). Do not mix it up with at lægge (to put something down).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ligge** i sengen og sove.
sentence.en: I want to lie in bed and sleep.

at ligge syg.explanation: "At ligge syg" means "to be ill in bed", too sick to get up: Min søn ligger syg med feber (My son is ill in bed with a fever). For being sick in general, say at være syg (to be sick).

forms.en: I have been ill in bed

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **ligge syg** hele ugen.
sentence.en: I cannot lie in bed sick all week.

at ligne.explanation: "At ligne" means "to look like", and it compares two things: Du ligner din far (You look like your father). To describe one person alone, say Du ser træt ud (You look tired).

sentence.da: Hun kan **ligne** sin mor, når hun smiler.
sentence.en: She can look like her mother when she smiles.

at like.explanation: "At like" means "to like (online)": Hun liker alle mine opslag (She likes all my posts). For liking a person, food or activity in real life, use at kunne lide (to like).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **like** dit billede på Instagram.
sentence.en: I will like your picture on Instagram.

at logge ind.explanation: "At logge ind" means "to log in", to enter an app or website with your username: Jeg logger ind hver morgen (I log in every morning). The opposite is at logge ud (to log out).

sentence.da: Du skal **logge ind** for at se dine beskeder.
sentence.en: You have to log in to see your messages.

at logge ud.explanation: "At logge ud" means "to log out", to leave your account when you are finished: Husk at logge ud på en fælles computer (Remember to log out on a shared computer).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **logge ud**, når jeg er færdig.
sentence.en: I want to log out when I am done.

at love.explanation: "At love" means "to promise": Jeg lover at komme (I promise to come). To say who gets the promise, put them right after the verb: Han lovede mig en gave (He promised me a gift).

sentence.da: Kan du **love** mig, at du kommer i morgen?
sentence.en: Can you promise me that you will come tomorrow?

at lufte hunden.explanation: "At lufte hunden" means "to walk the dog". It comes from lufte (to air out), so the idea is giving the dog fresh air: Jeg lufter hunden hver aften (I walk the dog every evening).

sentence.da: Hver morgen skal jeg **lufte hunden** i parken.
sentence.en: Every morning I have to walk the dog in the park.

at lufte ud.explanation: "At lufte ud" means "to air out", to let fresh air into a room: Vi lufter ud i stuen hver morgen (We air out the living room every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lufte ud**, fordi der lugter dårligt her.
sentence.en: I want to air out because it smells bad in here.

at lugte.explanation: "At lugte" means "to smell", both to give off a smell and to notice one: Blomsten lugter godt (The flower smells good). Jeg lugter røg (I smell smoke).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lugte** kaffe fra køkkenet.
sentence.en: I can smell coffee from the kitchen.

at lukke.explanation: "At lukke" means "to close", for a door, a window, a shop or a bag. Kan du lukke døren? means "Can you close the door?". In stores, you may hear Vi lukker om ti minutter (We close in ten minutes).

sentence.da: Kan du **lukke** vinduet? Det er koldt.
sentence.en: Can you close the window? It is cold.

at lyde.explanation: "At lyde" means "to sound", about how something seems when you hear it: Det lyder godt (That sounds good). Hun lyder glad (She sounds happy). Hearing itself is different: Jeg hører musik (I hear music).

sentence.da: Det kan **lyde** som en god idé.
sentence.en: It may sound like a good idea.

at lykkes.explanation: "At lykkes" means "to succeed" or "to work out", often with det (it) first: Det lykkedes mig at finde den (I managed to find it). A plan can work out too: Planen lykkedes (The plan worked).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, det vil **lykkes** mig at finde et job.
sentence.en: I hope I will succeed in finding a job.

at lyse.explanation: "At lyse" means "to shine" or "to give light": Månen lyser (The moon is shining). You can aim light at something with på (on): Jeg lyste på døren med lommelygten (I shone the flashlight on the door).

sentence.da: Lampen skal **lyse** i mørket.
sentence.en: The lamp has to shine in the dark.

at lyse op.explanation: "At lyse op" means "to light up": Hendes ansigt lyste op (Her face lit up). It also works for a lamp in a room: Lampen lyser rummet op (The lamp lights up the room).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt vil **lyse op**, når hun ser dig.
sentence.en: Her face will light up when she sees you.

at lytte.explanation: "At lytte" means "to listen" on purpose. At høre (to hear) is different: it is just noticing a sound, wanted or not. Compare Jeg hørte en lyd (I heard a sound) with Jeg lyttede til musikken (I listened to the music).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lytte** til musik og slappe af.
sentence.en: I want to listen to music and relax.

at lytte til.explanation: "At lytte til" means "to listen to", and you need til: Jeg lytter til radioen (I listen to the radio). At høre is just to hear: Jeg hørte dig ikke (I did not hear you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lytte til** musik i aften.
sentence.en: I want to listen to music tonight.

at lyve.explanation: "At lyve" means "to lie", as in telling a lie: Du lyver! (You are lying!) Lying down is a different word, at ligge (to lie): Jeg ligger i sengen (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **lyve** for mig.
sentence.en: You must not lie to me.

at låne.explanation: "At låne" means "to borrow" and also "to lend", so the situation tells you which. Kan jeg låne din pen? means "Can I borrow your pen?". Jeg låner dig min cykel means "I lend you my bike". To make it clear, Danes sometimes say låne af (borrow from) and låne ud (lend out).

sentence.da: Kan jeg **låne** din pen?
sentence.en: Can I borrow your pen?

at låse.explanation: "At låse" means "to lock": Han låser cyklen (He locks the bike). Adding op gives the opposite: at låse op (to unlock).

sentence.da: Husk at **låse** døren, når du går.
sentence.en: Remember to lock the door when you leave.

at låse op.explanation: "At låse op" means "to unlock". Put op after the thing you unlock: Hun låser skabet op (She unlocks the cabinet).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **låse op**, fordi jeg har glemt nøglen.
sentence.en: I cannot unlock because I have forgotten the key.

at lægge.explanation: "At lægge" means "to lay down": to put something down flat, like a book on a table or a baby in bed. Jeg lægger bogen på bordet means "I put the book on the table". Læg dig ned means "Lie down". Do not mix it up with at ligge (to be lying somewhere): Bogen ligger på bordet (The book is lying on the table).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lægge** bogen på bordet.
sentence.en: I want to put the book on the table.

at lægge fra sig.explanation: "At lægge fra sig" means "to put down" what you are holding: Han lagde bogen fra sig (He put the book down). Jeg lægger telefonen fra mig (I put the phone down).

sentence.da: Hun må **lægge fra sig**, hvad hun har i hænderne.
sentence.en: She has to put down what she has in her hands.

at lægge mærke til.explanation: "At lægge mærke til" means "to notice": Jeg lagde mærke til hans nye jakke (I noticed his new jacket). With aldrig (never), it describes someone who misses things: Han lægger aldrig mærke til noget (He never notices anything).

sentence.da: Hun vil nok **lægge mærke til** din nye frisure.
sentence.en: She will probably notice your new haircut.

at lægge planer.explanation: "At lægge planer" means "to make plans", often for a trip or an event: Hun lægger planer for en rejse (She is making plans for a trip).

sentence.da: Vi vil **lægge planer** for sommeren.
sentence.en: We want to make plans for the summer.

at lægge på.explanation: "At lægge på" means "to hang up", to end a phone call: Hun lagde på uden at sige farvel (She hung up without saying goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg må **lægge på**, fordi bussen kommer.
sentence.en: I have to hang up because the bus is coming.

at lægge sammen.explanation: "At lægge sammen" means "to add up": Jeg lægger to og tre sammen (I add two and three together). Sammen (together) comes after the numbers.

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lægge sammen** i hovedet.
sentence.en: I can add up in my head.

at lægge sig.explanation: "At lægge sig" means "to lie down": Jeg lægger mig på sofaen (I lie down on the sofa). To already be lying there, say at ligge (to lie): Jeg ligger i sengen (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Han er træt og vil **lægge sig** på sofaen.
sentence.en: He is tired and wants to lie down on the sofa.

at lære.explanation: "At lære" means "to learn" and also "to teach": Jeg lærer dansk (I learn Danish) and Hun lærer mig dansk (She teaches me Danish). En lærer (a teacher) looks just like lærer in jeg lærer. Do not mix it up with at læse (to read).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lære** dansk i år.
sentence.en: I want to learn Danish this year.

at lære at kende.explanation: "At lære at kende" means "to get to know" a person: Jeg lærer ham at kende (I am getting to know him). The person goes in the middle: Vi lærte hinanden at kende i Aarhus (We got to know each other in Aarhus).

forms.da: jeg har lært ham at kende
forms.en: I have gotten to know him

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at **lære at kende** nye mennesker.
sentence.en: It is nice to get to know new people.

at lære udenad.explanation: "At lære udenad" means "to memorize", to learn something by heart so you can say it without looking: Jeg lærer ordene udenad (I memorize the words). Plain at lære (to learn) does not mean by heart.

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **lære udenad** til prøven i morgen.
sentence.en: The students have to memorize for the test tomorrow.

at læse.explanation: "At læse" means "to read": Jeg læser en bog (I am reading a book). It also means to study a subject at university: Hun læser medicin (She studies medicine). Do not mix it up with at lære (to learn).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **læse** en bog i aften.
sentence.en: I want to read a book tonight.

at læse om.explanation: "At læse om" means "to read about" a topic: Jeg læser om dansk historie (I am reading about Danish history). Reading the book itself is just at læse (to read): Jeg læser en bog (I am reading a book).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **læse om** Island.
sentence.en: I would like to read about Iceland.

at læse op.explanation: "At læse op" means "to read aloud" to other people: Læreren læser op for klassen (The teacher reads aloud to the class). It also means to read out a list: Han læste navnene op (He read out the names).

sentence.da: Kan du **læse op** for os?
sentence.en: Can you read aloud to us?

at læse til.explanation: "At læse til" means "to study to become", and the job comes right after til: Han læser til læge (He is studying to become a doctor). Without til, at læse alone means "to read" or "to study".

sentence.da: Min søster vil **læse til** læge i København.
sentence.en: My sister wants to study to become a doctor in Copenhagen.

at løbe.explanation: "At løbe" means "to run", for sport or in a hurry: Jeg løber hver morgen (I run every morning). It is also used for a nose or a river that flows: Min næse løber (My nose is running). At løbe tør for means "to run out of".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **løbe** hurtigt for at nå bussen.
sentence.en: I want to run fast to catch the bus.

at løbe efter.explanation: "At løbe efter" means "to run after": Hunden løber efter bolden (The dog runs after the ball). For a real chase, use at jage (to chase): Katten jager musen (The cat chases the mouse).

sentence.da: Jeg måtte **løbe efter** bussen i morges.
sentence.en: I had to run after the bus this morning.

at løbe en tur.explanation: "At løbe en tur" means "to go for a run": Jeg løber en tur efter arbejde (I go for a run after work). The same pattern works for other trips: at gå en tur (to go for a walk).

forms.en: I have gone for a run

related.en: to go for a bike ride

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, vil jeg **løbe en tur**.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, I want to go for a run.

at løbe ind i.explanation: "At løbe ind i" means "to run into", both a thing and a person: Jeg løb ind i en dør (I ran into a door). For meeting someone by chance: Jeg løb ind i min nabo (I ran into my neighbor).

sentence.da: I byen kan jeg **løbe ind i** en gammel ven.
sentence.en: In town I might run into an old friend.

at løbe på skøjter.explanation: "At løbe på skøjter" means "to ice-skate". It is built from løbe (run) and på skøjter (on skates): Hun løber på skøjter hver vinter (She ice-skates every winter).

sentence.da: Om vinteren kan vi **løbe på skøjter** på isen.
sentence.en: In winter we can ice-skate on the ice.

at løbe tør for.explanation: "At løbe tør for" means "to run out of", when you have none left: Vi løb tør for mælk (We ran out of milk). What you run out of comes after for: Hun løber tør for tid (She is running out of time).

sentence.da: Vi vil snart **løbe tør for** mælk.
sentence.en: We will soon run out of milk.

at løbe væk.explanation: "At løbe væk" means "to run away": Drengen løb væk fra hunden (The boy ran away from the dog). Hunden løb væk (The dog ran away).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **løbe væk**, når vi åbner døren.
sentence.en: The dog will run away when we open the door.

at løfte.explanation: "At løfte" means "to lift" and "to raise": Jeg løfter barnet (I lift the child). Hun løfter armen (She raises her arm). Watch out for et løfte, which is a promise: Jeg giver dig et løfte (I give you a promise).

sentence.da: Han kan **løfte** tunge ting alene.
sentence.en: He can lift heavy things alone.

at løse.explanation: "At løse" means "to solve": Jeg løser opgaven (I solve the task). It also means "to untie": Hun løste knuden (She untied the knot).

sentence.da: Vi kan **løse** problemet sammen.
sentence.en: We can solve the problem together.

en ladcykel.explanation: "En ladcykel" means "a cargo bike", a bike with a big box on the front for kids or shopping: Tre børn kan sidde i en ladcykel (Three kids can sit in a cargo bike).

sentence.da: Der er plads til mange indkøb i min **ladcykel**.
sentence.en: There is room for a lot of groceries in my cargo bike.

en lade.explanation: "En lade" means "a barn", where a farmer keeps hay and machines: Der er hø i laden (There is hay in the barn). Do not mix it up with at lade (to let), which is spelled the same.

sentence.da: Bonden har hø og maskiner i sin **lade**.
sentence.en: The farmer keeps hay and machines in his barn.

en ladestander.explanation: "En ladestander" means "a charging station", the post where you plug in an electric car. It is built from lade (charge) and stander (post): Er ladestanderen ledig? (Is the charging station free?)

sentence.da: Jeg parkerer ved en **ladestander** og lader min bil.
sentence.en: I park at a charging station and charge my car.

en lagkage.explanation: "En lagkage" means "a layer cake". It is built from et lag (a layer) and en kage (a cake), with cream or jam between the layers of sponge cake: Hun bager en lagkage (She is baking a layer cake).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **lagkage** med fløde til fødselsdagen.
sentence.en: We eat layer cake with cream for the birthday.

en lampe.explanation: "En lampe" means "a lamp". Tænd lampen means "Turn on the lamp", and sluk lampen means "Turn off the lamp".

sentence.da: Det er mørkt, jeg tænder en **lampe**.
sentence.en: It is dark, so I switch on a lamp.

en lampeskærm.explanation: "En lampeskærm" means "a lampshade", the cover around the light: Lampeskærmen er hvid (The lampshade is white). Jeg støver lampeskærmen af (I dust the lampshade).

sentence.da: Pæren er skjult bag en gul **lampeskærm**.
sentence.en: The bulb is hidden behind a yellow lampshade.

en landevej.explanation: "En landevej" means "a country road", a road between towns outside the big cities. It is slower than a highway: Vi kører ad landevejen i stedet for motorvejen (We take the country road instead of the highway).

sentence.da: Vi kører langsomt på en smal **landevej**.
sentence.en: We drive slowly on a narrow country road.

en landing.explanation: "En landing" means "a landing", mostly for a plane touching down: Landingen var rolig (The landing was smooth). It comes from at lande (to land).

sentence.da: Flyet havde en rolig **landing** i Kastrup.
sentence.en: The plane had a smooth landing in Kastrup.

en landingsbane.explanation: "En landingsbane" means "a runway", the long strip at an airport. It is built from landing (landing) and bane (track): Flyet venter på landingsbanen (The plane waits on the runway).

sentence.da: Flyet lander på en lang **landingsbane**.
sentence.en: The plane lands on a long runway.

en landmand.explanation: "En landmand" means "a farmer", built from land (countryside) and mand (man). Danish leaves out a for jobs: Han er landmand means "He is a farmer".

sentence.da: En **landmand** har køer og arbejder på marken.
sentence.en: A farmer has cows and works in the field.

en landsby.explanation: "En landsby" means "a village", a small place in the countryside: Min farmor bor i en lille landsby (My grandmother lives in a small village). Landsbyen har kun en butik (The village has only one shop).

sentence.da: Der bor kun hundrede mennesker i vores **landsby**.
sentence.en: Only a hundred people live in our village.

en lastbil.explanation: "En lastbil" means "a truck", a large vehicle for carrying goods: Lastbilen kører med mælk (The truck is carrying milk). It is built from last (load) and bil (car).

sentence.da: Der holder en stor **lastbil** foran huset.
sentence.en: A big truck is parked in front of the house.

en lastbilchauffør.explanation: "En lastbilchauffør" means "a truck driver". It is built from en lastbil (a truck) and en chauffør (a driver): En lastbilchauffør kører varer til butikker (A truck driver drives goods to stores).

sentence.da: Min far er **lastbilchauffør** og kører meget.
sentence.en: My father is a truck driver and drives a lot.

en leder.explanation: "En leder" means "a leader" or "a manager", someone who guides a team: Vores leder hjælper os (Our leader helps us). For the top person of a whole company, use en direktør (a director).

sentence.da: Vores **leder** er altid venlig og hjælper os.
sentence.en: Our leader is always friendly and helps us.

en ledning.explanation: "En ledning" means "a cord" or "a cable" that carries electricity: Ledningen er for kort (The cord is too short). Jeg trækker ledningen ud (I pull out the cord).

sentence.da: Pas på, der ligger en **ledning** på gulvet.
sentence.en: Watch out, there is a cord on the floor.

en leg.explanation: "En leg" means "a game" in the sense of play, mostly for children: Børn elsker en god leg (Children love a good game). For a board game or sports game, use et spil (a game): Vi spiller et spil (We play a game).

sentence.da: Børnene har fundet på en ny **leg**.
sentence.en: The children have invented a new game.

en legeplads.explanation: "En legeplads" means "a playground", a place with swings and slides for children: Vi mødes på legepladsen efter skole (We meet at the playground after school).

sentence.da: Børnene løber rundt og leger på en **legeplads**.
sentence.en: The children run around and play on a playground.

en lejekontrakt.explanation: "En lejekontrakt" means "a lease", the written agreement for renting a home. It is built from at leje (to rent) and en kontrakt (a contract): Vi skal skrive under på lejekontrakten (We have to sign the lease).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **lejekontrakt** på to år.
sentence.en: I have a lease for two years.

en lejer.explanation: "En lejer" means "a tenant", the person who rents a home from the owner. The other side is en udlejer (a landlord): En lejer og en udlejer skriver under (A tenant and a landlord sign).

sentence.da: Jeg er **lejer** og ejer ikke lejligheden.
sentence.en: I am a tenant and do not own the apartment.

en lejlighed.explanation: "En lejlighed" means "an apartment" or "a flat". At leje en lejlighed means "to rent an apartment". En lejlighed med tre værelser means "an apartment with three rooms".

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lille **lejlighed**.
sentence.en: We live in a small apartment.

en lejr.explanation: "En lejr" means "a camp", a place where people stay for a while: Klassen tager på lejr (The class goes to camp). To set up a camp, say at slå lejr (to pitch camp).

sentence.da: Børnene sover i telte i vores **lejr**.
sentence.en: The kids sleep in tents in our camp.

en lektion.explanation: "En lektion" means "a lesson", one class period at school: Vi har en lektion i engelsk (We have a lesson in English). Do not mix it up with lektier (homework): Jeg laver lektier (I do homework).

sentence.da: Den næste **lektion** begynder om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The next lesson begins in five minutes.

en leopard.explanation: "En leopard" means "a leopard", a big spotted wild cat. It looks like a cheetah (en gepard), but a leopard is heavier and often climbs trees: Leoparden sover i et træ (The leopard sleeps in a tree).

sentence.da: En **leopard** klatrer op i træet og sover.
sentence.en: A leopard climbs up the tree and sleeps.

en letbane.explanation: "En letbane" means "a light rail", an electric train that looks like a tram. It runs on streets in town and faster out in the country: Letbanen er hurtigere end bussen (The light rail is faster than the bus).

sentence.da: Der kører en **letbane** gennem Aarhus.
sentence.en: A light rail runs through Aarhus.

en levering.explanation: "En levering" means "a delivery", goods brought to you: Leveringen tager to dage (The delivery takes two days).

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **levering** fra butikken.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a delivery from the store.

en lift.explanation: "En lift" means "a ride in someone's car". You ask for one with Kan jeg få en lift hjem? (Can I get a ride home?) and offer one with Jeg kan give dig en lift (I can give you a ride).

forms.en: I will give you a ride

sentence.da: Kan jeg få en **lift** til stationen?
sentence.en: Can I get a ride to the station?

en lighter.explanation: "En lighter" means "a lighter", the small thing that makes a flame: Har du en lighter? (Do you have a lighter?). A match is en tændstik (a match).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tænde bålet uden min **lighter**.
sentence.en: I can't light the fire without my lighter.

en lillebror.explanation: "En lillebror" means "a little brother", a brother who is younger than you. It is built from lille (little) and en bror (a brother).

sentence.da: Min **lillebror** er fem år.
sentence.en: My little brother is five years old.

en lillesøster.explanation: "En lillesøster" means "a little sister", a sister who is younger than you. It is built from lille (little) and en søster (a sister).

sentence.da: Min **lillesøster** er tre år.
sentence.en: My little sister is three years old.

en lime.explanation: "En lime" means "a lime", a small green fruit. Do not mix it up with en citron (a lemon), which is yellow: Citronen er gul (The lemon is yellow).

sentence.da: Jeg presser en **lime** over fisken.
sentence.en: I squeeze a lime over the fish.

en lineal.explanation: "En lineal" means "a ruler", the tool for measuring and drawing straight lines: Jeg tegner en streg med en lineal (I draw a line with a ruler). A ruler who rules a country is en hersker.

sentence.da: Jeg måler papiret med en **lineal**.
sentence.en: I measure the paper with a ruler.

en linje.explanation: "En linje" means "a line": Tegn en linje (Draw a line). It is also a bus or train line: Tag linje 5 (Take line 5). For people waiting in a line, say en kø (a queue).

sentence.da: Tegn en lige **linje** på papiret.
sentence.en: Draw a straight line on the paper.

en liste.explanation: "En liste" means "a list". At skrive noget på listen means "to write something on the list".

sentence.da: Jeg skriver mælk og brød på en **liste**.
sentence.en: I write milk and bread on a list.

en liter.explanation: "En liter" means "a liter". Tre liter vand means "three liters of water".

sentence.da: Jeg køber to **liter** mælk.
sentence.en: I am buying two liters of milk.

en livredder.explanation: "En livredder" means "a lifeguard", a person who watches swimmers and saves them if needed: Livredderen sidder i tårnet (The lifeguard sits in the tower). It is built from liv (life) and redder (rescuer).

sentence.da: En **livredder** passer på børnene ved vandet.
sentence.en: A lifeguard watches the children by the water.

en livret.explanation: "En livret" means "a favorite dish", the meal you love most: Hvad er din livret? (What is your favorite dish?). It is built from liv (life) and ret (dish).

sentence.da: Min **livret** er lasagne, og jeg elsker den.
sentence.en: My favorite dish is lasagna, and I love it.

en livsstil.explanation: "En livsstil" means "a lifestyle", the way a person lives: en sund livsstil (a healthy lifestyle). It is built from liv (life) and stil (style).

sentence.da: Hun har en meget sund **livsstil**.
sentence.en: She has a very healthy lifestyle.

en lobby.explanation: "En lobby" means "a lobby", the big entrance hall of a hotel or an office building: Vi mødes i lobbyen (We are meeting in the lobby).

sentence.da: Vi venter i hotellets **lobby**.
sentence.en: We are waiting in the hotel's lobby.

en loftslampe.explanation: "En loftslampe" means "a ceiling light". It is built from loft (ceiling) and lampe (lamp): Loftslampen hænger over bordet (The ceiling light hangs over the table).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **loftslampe** i stuen.
sentence.en: We have a big ceiling light in the living room.

en lomme.explanation: "En lomme" means "a pocket". Det er i min lomme means "It is in my pocket", and Jeg har hænderne i lommerne means "I have my hands in my pockets".

sentence.da: Mine nøgler er i min **lomme**.
sentence.en: My keys are in my pocket.

en lommelygte.explanation: "En lommelygte" means "a flashlight". It is built from lomme (pocket) and lygte (light), so it is literally a pocket light: Tag en lommelygte med (Bring a flashlight).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **lommelygte**, fordi det er mørkt.
sentence.en: I use a flashlight because it is dark.

en lommeregner.explanation: "En lommeregner" means "a calculator". It is built from lomme (pocket) and regne (calculate): Må jeg låne din lommeregner? (May I borrow your calculator?)

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **lommeregner** til matematik.
sentence.en: I use a calculator for math.

en lov.explanation: "En lov" means "a law", a rule that everyone in a country must follow: Det er imod loven at stjæle (It is against the law to steal). Politiet passer på, at vi følger lovene (The police make sure we follow the laws).

sentence.da: Der er en ny **lov** om cykelhjelme.
sentence.en: There is a new law about bicycle helmets.

en lufthavn.explanation: "En lufthavn" means "an airport". It is built from luft (air) and havn (harbor), so it is literally an air harbor. I lufthavnen means "at the airport".

sentence.da: Flyene lander og letter i en stor **lufthavn**.
sentence.en: The planes land and take off at a big airport.

en lugt.explanation: "En lugt" means "a smell", good or bad: Der er en dårlig lugt i badeværelset (There is a bad smell in the bathroom). For a nice smell, you can say en duft (a scent).

sentence.da: Der er en dejlig **lugt** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a lovely smell in the kitchen.

en lunge.explanation: "En lunge" means "a lung", the body part you breathe with. Man har to lunger (A person has two lungs). Lungebetændelse means "pneumonia".

sentence.da: Lægen kiggede på billedet af min **lunge**.
sentence.en: The doctor looked at the picture of my lung.

en lup.explanation: "En lup" means "a magnifying glass", which makes small things look bigger: Jeg læser den lille tekst med en lup (I read the small text with a magnifying glass).

sentence.da: Teksten er lille, så jeg bruger en **lup**.
sentence.en: The text is small, so I use a magnifying glass.

en lyd.explanation: "En lyd" means "a sound", anything you hear: Jeg hører en mærkelig lyd (I hear a strange sound). It also means the volume on a device: Skru op for lyden (Turn up the sound).

sentence.da: Vi hørte en høj **lyd** i natten.
sentence.en: We heard a loud sound in the night.

en lygte.explanation: "En lygte" means "a light", such as a bike light or a lantern: Cyklen skal have en lygte (The bike must have a light). A lamp in a room is en lampe (a lamp).

sentence.da: Når det bliver mørkt, tænder jeg min **lygte**.
sentence.en: When it gets dark, I turn on my light.

en lynlås.explanation: "En lynlås" means "a zipper": Min jakke har en lynlås (My jacket has a zipper). To zip up, say at lukke lynlåsen (to close the zipper).

sentence.da: Jakken har en **lynlås** foran, ikke knapper.
sentence.en: The jacket has a zipper in front, not buttons.

en lyskontakt.explanation: "En lyskontakt" means "a light switch". It is built from lys (light) and kontakt (switch, contact): Tryk på lyskontakten (Press the light switch).

sentence.da: Der er en **lyskontakt** ved siden af døren.
sentence.en: There is a light switch next to the door.

en lyspære.explanation: "En lyspære" means "a lightbulb". It is built from lys (light) and pære (pear), because of its shape: Jeg skal skifte en lyspære (I have to change a lightbulb).

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **lyspære** til lampen.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new lightbulb for the lamp.

en låge.explanation: "En låge" means "a gate", a small gate in a fence or hedge: Luk lågen, når du går (Close the gate when you leave). A big gate, for example for cars, is en port (a gate).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **låge** ind til haven.
sentence.en: There is a small gate into the garden.

en lås.explanation: "En lås" means "a lock", on a door, a bike or a suitcase: Døren har en ny lås (The door has a new lock). The action is different: at låse (to lock).

sentence.da: Jeg sætter en **lås** på min cykel.
sentence.en: I put a lock on my bike.

en læbe.explanation: "En læbe" means "a lip". Røde læber means "red lips" and tørre læber means "dry lips". Words like en læbestift (a lipstick) are built from it.

sentence.da: Jeg har et lille sår på min **læbe**.
sentence.en: I have a small cut on my lip.

en læbestift.explanation: "En læbestift" means "a lipstick". It is built from læbe (lip) and stift (stick): Hun har rød læbestift på (She is wearing red lipstick).

sentence.da: Hun tager rød **læbestift** på.
sentence.en: She puts on red lipstick.

en læge.explanation: "En læge" means "a doctor". At gå til lægen means "to go to the doctor".

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og ser en **læge**.
sentence.en: I am ill and see a doctor.

en lænestol.explanation: "En lænestol" means "an armchair", a soft chair you lean back in: Jeg læser i lænestolen (I read in the armchair). A normal chair at the table is en stol (a chair).

sentence.da: Han sidder i en **lænestol** og læser avis.
sentence.en: He sits in an armchair and reads the newspaper.

en længde.explanation: "En længde" means "a length": Kan du måle længden? (Can you measure the length?) In a pool, it is one trip from end to end: Jeg svømmer ti længder (I swim ten lengths).

sentence.da: Bordets **længde** er to meter.
sentence.en: The table's length is two meters.

en lærebog.explanation: "En lærebog" means "a textbook", a book you learn from. It is built from at lære (to learn) and en bog (a book): Åbn din lærebog på side ti (Open your textbook to page ten).

sentence.da: Min **lærebog** i dansk er meget tyk.
sentence.en: My Danish textbook is very thick.

en lærer.explanation: "En lærer" means "a teacher", for a man or a woman. To say what someone does for a living, you leave out en: Hun er lærer means "She is a teacher".

sentence.da: Vores **lærer** underviser os i dansk i skolen.
sentence.en: Our teacher teaches us Danish at school.

en læser.explanation: "En læser" means "a reader", a person who reads books or newspapers: Bogen har mange læsere (The book has many readers). Du er en god læser (You are a good reader).

sentence.da: Hun er en flittig **læser** og låner mange bøger.
sentence.en: She is a diligent reader and borrows many books.

en løbesko.explanation: "En løbesko" means "a running shoe", a shoe made for jogging and sport: Jeg har købt nye løbesko (I have bought new running shoes). It is built from løbe (run) and sko (shoe).

sentence.da: Jeg har nye **løbesko**, så jeg løber en tur.
sentence.en: I have new running shoes, so I am going for a run.

en løbetur.explanation: "En løbetur" means "a run", a jog for exercise: Jeg tager en løbetur før arbejde (I go for a run before work). It is built from løbe (to run) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **løbetur** i parken hver morgen.
sentence.en: I go for a run in the park every morning.

en løgn.explanation: "En løgn" means "a lie", something untrue that someone says on purpose: Det er en løgn! (That is a lie!) To tell a lie, use at fortælle: Han fortalte en løgn (He told a lie).

sentence.da: Det er en **løgn**, og det ved du godt.
sentence.en: That is a lie, and you know it.

en løn.explanation: "En løn" means "a salary", the money you get for work: Hendes løn er høj (Her salary is high). Pay for one hour is timeløn (hourly pay).

sentence.da: Jeg får min **løn** den første i måneden.
sentence.en: I get my salary on the first of the month.

en løsning.explanation: "En løsning" means "a solution", for a problem or a puzzle: Vi har brug for en løsning (We need a solution). The matching verb is at løse (to solve): Jeg kan løse opgaven (I can solve the task).

sentence.da: Vi har et problem og leder efter en **løsning**.
sentence.en: We have a problem and are looking for a solution.

en løve.explanation: "En løve" means "a lion". Løven sover i solen means "The lion sleeps in the sun". A female lion is en løvinde (a lioness).

sentence.da: En **løve** brøler højt.
sentence.en: A lion roars loudly.

et lag.explanation: "Et lag" means "a layer", one level on top of another: Kagen har tre lag (The cake has three layers). It is also the start of en lagkage (a layer cake).

sentence.da: Der ligger et tykt **lag** sne på taget.
sentence.en: There is a thick layer of snow on the roof.

et lagen.explanation: "Et lagen" means "a sheet" for a bed: Jeg skifter lagenet (I change the sheet). A sheet of paper is not a lagen but et ark (a sheet of paper).

sentence.da: Jeg skal skifte **lagen** på sengen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to change the sheet on the bed today.

et lam.explanation: "Et lam" means "a lamb", a young sheep: Lammet er ude på marken (The lamb is out in the field). It is also the meat: Jeg elsker lam (I love lamb).

sentence.da: Et lille **lam** går ved siden af sin mor.
sentence.en: A little lamb walks beside its mother.

et land.explanation: "Et land" means "a country", and it can also mean "land" or "countryside". På landet means "in the countryside".

sentence.da: Danmark er et lille **land**.
sentence.en: Denmark is a small country.

et landbrug.explanation: "Et landbrug" means "a farm" as a business, and also "agriculture" as a whole: Der er meget landbrug i Danmark (There is a lot of agriculture in Denmark). The farmhouse and yard is en gård (a farm).

sentence.da: Min onkel har et **landbrug** med køer og grise.
sentence.en: My uncle has a farm with cows and pigs.

et landkort.explanation: "Et landkort" means "a map", a map of a country or a region: Vi finder vejen på landkortet (We find the way on the map). The short form et kort (a map) can also mean "a card".

sentence.da: Der hænger et **landkort** på væggen.
sentence.en: There is a map hanging on the wall.

et landshold.explanation: "Et landshold" means "a national team", the team that plays for a whole country: Han spiller på landsholdet (He plays on the national team). It is built from land (country) and hold (team).

sentence.da: Vores **landshold** vandt kampen i går.
sentence.en: Our national team won the match yesterday.

et landskab.explanation: "Et landskab" means "a landscape", the land around you: Det danske landskab er fladt (The Danish landscape is flat). For the view from one spot, use en udsigt (a view).

sentence.da: Vi kørte gennem et flot **landskab**.
sentence.en: We drove through a beautiful landscape.

et like.explanation: "Et like" means "a like", the thumbs-up on social media: Billedet fik hundrede likes (The picture got a hundred likes). To give one, say at give et like (to give a like).

sentence.da: Mit billede fik et **like** fra min mor.
sentence.en: My picture got a like from my mom.

et link.explanation: "Et link" means "a link" on a web page or in a message: Jeg sender dig et link (I am sending you a link). Hvor er linket? (Where is the link?)

sentence.da: Klik på det **link** for at se videoen.
sentence.en: Click on that link to see the video.

et liv.explanation: "Et liv" means "a life", both one person's life and life in general: livet er godt means "life is good", and "at have et godt liv" means "to have a good life".

sentence.da: Vi har kun ét **liv**.
sentence.en: We only have one life.

et loft.explanation: "Et loft" means "a ceiling" or "an attic": Der er en lampe i loftet (There is a lamp in the ceiling). Vi har gamle ting på loftet (We have old things in the attic).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en lejlighed med et højt **loft**.
sentence.en: We live in an apartment with a high ceiling.

et loppemarked.explanation: "Et loppemarked" means "a flea market", where people sell used things: Vi sælger gamle bøger på et loppemarked (We sell old books at a flea market). To go there, say at gå på loppemarked (to go to a flea market).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en gammel lampe på et **loppemarked**.
sentence.en: I found an old lamp at a flea market.

et lykønskningskort.explanation: "Et lykønskningskort" means "a congratulations card", sent for a birthday, a wedding or a new baby: Vi sendte et lykønskningskort til dem (We sent them a congratulations card). It is built from lykønskning (congratulation) and kort (card).

sentence.da: Vi sendte et **lykønskningskort** til de nygifte.
sentence.en: We sent a congratulations card to the newlyweds.

et lyskryds.explanation: "Et lyskryds" means "an intersection with traffic lights": Bilerne venter i lyskrydset (The cars wait at the intersection). One without lights is just et vejkryds (an intersection).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved det næste **lyskryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection with traffic lights.

et lån.explanation: "Et lån" means "a loan", money you borrow and pay back: Jeg tager et lån til en bil (I take out a loan for a car). The word at låne means both "to borrow" and "to lend": Jeg låner dig en pen (I lend you a pen).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have et **lån**, når jeg køber huset.
sentence.en: I need a loan when I buy the house.

et lår.explanation: "Et lår" means "a thigh", the top part of your leg. It is also used in cooking: et kyllingelår is a chicken thigh.

sentence.da: Mit **lår** er over mit knæ.
sentence.en: My thigh is above my knee.

et løfte.explanation: "Et løfte" means "a promise": Han gav mig et løfte (He gave me a promise). You keep one with at holde (to hold): Jeg holder mit løfte (I keep my promise). To break one, use at bryde (to break): Han brød sit løfte (He broke his promise).

sentence.da: Jeg gav ham et **løfte**, og jeg holdt det.
sentence.en: I gave him a promise, and I kept it.

et løg.explanation: "Et løg" means "an onion". It is also part of hvidløg (garlic), which is literally white onion.

sentence.da: Jeg skærer et **løg** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: I cut an onion in the kitchen.

lad os se.explanation: "Lad os se" means "let's see", and you say it while you think, check something or wait for a result. Lad works like let, so lad os gå (let's go) is built the same way.

forms.da: Lad os se, hvad klokken er.
forms.en: Let's see what time it is.

forms.da: Lad os se, om han kommer.

sentence.da: **Lad os se** i køleskabet.
sentence.en: Let's look in the fridge.

lad være.explanation: "Lad være" means "don't" or "leave it". Add med at before what you should not do: Lad være med at ringe (Don't call). On its own, Lad være! means "Don't!".

forms.da: Lad være med at spise det

sentence.da: **Lad være** med at røre ved kagen!
sentence.en: Don't touch the cake!

lakrids.explanation: "Lakrids" means "licorice", the black, chewy candy: Jeg elsker lakrids (I love licorice). It is also used in ice cream: lakridsis (licorice ice cream).

sentence.da: **Lakrids** er sort og lidt salt.
sentence.en: Licorice is black and a little salty.

laks.explanation: "Laks" means "salmon". For one fish, you can say en laks (a salmon), but as food there is no en: Jeg spiser laks (I eat salmon).

sentence.da: **Laks** er en lyserød fisk.
sentence.en: Salmon is a pink fish.

laktosefri.explanation: "Laktosefri" means "lactose-free". It is built from laktose (lactose) and fri (free), so it tells you what the food leaves out: laktosefri mælk (lactose-free milk).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker kun **laktosefri** mælk.
sentence.en: I only drink lactose-free milk.

lammekød.explanation: "Lammekød" means "lamb" as meat. It is built from et lam (a lamb) and kød (meat). The animal is et lam: Der er et lam på marken (There is a lamb in the field).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **lammekød** med kartofler i aften.
sentence.en: We eat lamb with potatoes tonight.

lang.explanation: "Lang" means "long", in distance or in time. Langt on its own also means "far": Det er langt væk (It is far away).

sentence.da: Det er en **lang** vej.
sentence.en: It is a long way.

langs.explanation: "Langs" means "along" and shows moving or lying next to a line, like a road or a shore: Vi går langs stranden (We walk along the beach). It can also come after the thing: Vi går stranden langs (We walk along the beach).

sentence.da: Vi går **langs** vandet hver aften.
sentence.en: We walk along the water every evening.

langsom.explanation: "Langsom" means "slow". To say that something happens slowly, use langsomt: Tal langsomt, tak (Speak slowly, please).

sentence.da: Skildpadden er meget **langsom**.
sentence.en: The turtle is very slow.

langt fra.explanation: "Langt fra" means "far from", and a place follows it: Hotellet er langt fra byen (The hotel is far from the town). Compare langt væk (far away), which stands alone: Hotellet er langt væk (The hotel is far away). Langt fra! on its own means "Far from it!".

forms.en: The hotel is far from the town.

sentence.da: Vores hus ligger **langt fra** byen.
sentence.en: Our house is far from the town.

langt væk.explanation: "Langt væk" means "far away" and stands alone: Hun bor langt væk (She lives far away). Compare langt fra (far from), which needs a place after it: Hun bor langt fra byen (She lives far from the town).

sentence.da: Min familie bor **langt væk**.
sentence.en: My family lives far away.

larm.explanation: "Larm" means "noise", a loud sound that bothers you: Børnene laver meget larm (The children make a lot of noise). Støj (noise) is close in meaning and often used for traffic and machines.

sentence.da: Der er for meget **larm** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is too much noise on the street.

latterlig.explanation: "Latterlig" means "ridiculous", for something so silly or unreasonable that it is almost funny or annoying: Det er latterligt dyrt (That is ridiculously expensive).

sentence.da: Det er en **latterlig** pris for en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: That is a ridiculous price for a cup of coffee.

lav.explanation: "Lav" means "low", and it is also used for a person who is short. It works for prices too: lave priser means "low prices".

sentence.da: Stolen er meget **lav**.
sentence.en: The chair is very low.

ledig.explanation: "Ledig" means "vacant" or "available" and fits a seat, a room, a job or free time: Er bordet ledigt? (Is the table free?). Someone without a job is also ledig.

sentence.da: Er der en **ledig** plads her?
sentence.en: Is there a free seat here?

legetøj.explanation: "Legetøj" means "toys", all your toys together: Mit legetøj er i kassen (My toys are in the box). For one toy, name it, like en bamse (a teddy bear).

sentence.da: Barnet leger med sit **legetøj**.
sentence.en: The child plays with their toys.

leggings.explanation: "Leggings" means "leggings", the stretchy pants that fit tight on the legs: Jeg løber i leggings (I run in leggings). It is always plural, so one pair is et par leggings (a pair of leggings).

sentence.da: Hun løber i sorte **leggings** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She runs in black leggings every morning.

lektier.explanation: "Lektier" means "homework". It goes with at lave (to do, to make): Jeg laver lektier (I do my homework). Mange lektier means "a lot of homework". En lektie (one piece of homework) is rarely used.

sentence.da: Efter skole sidder jeg og laver **lektier**.
sentence.en: After school I sit and do homework.

let.explanation: "Let" means "easy" or "light in weight": en let opgave (an easy task) and en let taske (a light bag). The situation shows which one you mean.

sentence.da: Opgaven er meget **let**.
sentence.en: The task is very easy.

letmælk.explanation: "Letmælk" means "low-fat milk", milk with less fat than whole milk: Jeg tager letmælk i kaffen (I take low-fat milk in my coffee). It is built from let (light) and mælk (milk).

sentence.da: Vi køber **letmælk**, fordi den har mindre fedt.
sentence.en: We buy low-fat milk because it has less fat.

lettelse.explanation: "Lettelse" means "relief", the good feeling when a worry is gone: Det var en lettelse (That was a relief). Someone who feels it is lettet (relieved): Jeg er så lettet (I am so relieved).

sentence.da: Jeg sukkede af **lettelse**, fordi prøven var slut.
sentence.en: I sighed with relief because the test was over.

lettere.explanation: "Lettere" means "easier" and "lighter": Danish bliver lettere hver dag (Danish gets easier every day). It comes from let (easy / light): Tasken er let (The bag is light).

sentence.da: Det bliver **lettere** at tale dansk hver dag.
sentence.en: It gets easier to speak Danish every day.

lettet.explanation: "Lettet" means "relieved", how you feel when a worry goes away: Hun var lettet over, at eksamen var overstået (She was relieved that the exam was over).

sentence.da: Jeg var **lettet**, da hun ringede.
sentence.en: I was relieved when she called.

levende.explanation: "Levende" means "alive" or "living": et levende dyr (a living animal). For music it means "live": levende musik (live music).

sentence.da: Vi hørte **levende** musik på caféen i går.
sentence.en: We heard live music at the café yesterday.

leverpostej.explanation: "Leverpostej" means "liver pâté", a soft spread for bread: Hun smører leverpostej på brødet (She spreads liver pâté on the bread). It is built from lever (liver) and postej (pâté).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg **leverpostej** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch I eat liver pâté on rye bread.

lidt.explanation: "Lidt" means "a little" or "a bit": lidt mælk (a little milk), lidt træt (a bit tired). Do not mix it up with lille (small): en lille kop (a small cup) is about size, while lidt vand (a little water) is about amount.

sentence.da: Jeg vil kun have **lidt** mad.
sentence.en: I only want a little food.

lidt efter lidt.explanation: "Lidt efter lidt" means "little by little" and describes slow, steady change: Lidt efter lidt lærer jeg dansk (Little by little, I am learning Danish). Word for word, it is a little after a little.

forms.da: lidt efter lidt bliver det bedre
forms.en: little by little it gets better

sentence.da: **Lidt efter lidt** forstår jeg flere ord.
sentence.en: Little by little, I understand more words.

lidt langsommere, tak.explanation: "Lidt langsommere, tak" means "a bit slower, please". Langsommere means slower (from langsom, slow). If you also missed the words, add Kan du sige det igen? (Can you say that again?).

forms.en: Can you speak a bit slower?

sentence.da: Du taler for hurtigt. **Lidt langsommere, tak**!
sentence.en: You speak too fast. A bit slower, please!

lige.explanation: "Lige" means "straight" or "equal", and in et lige tal it means "even" (2, 4, 6). It is also used for "just" or "right": lige nu means "right now" and "lige ved siden af" means "right next to".

sentence.da: Stregen er meget **lige**.
sentence.en: The line is very straight.

lige meget hvad.explanation: "Lige meget hvad" means "no matter what" and says that something stays the same whatever happens: Jeg elsker dig lige meget hvad (I love you no matter what). To be specific, add der sker (happens).

forms.en: I am coming no matter what.

forms.da: Lige meget hvad der sker, ringer jeg.
forms.en: No matter what happens, I will call.

sentence.da: Jeg kommer til dig **lige meget hvad**.
sentence.en: I will come to you no matter what.

lige nu.explanation: "Lige nu" means "right now". It is built from lige (just) and nu (now). For something a little later, use om lidt (in a little while).

forms.en: What are you doing right now?

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke tid **lige nu**.
sentence.en: I do not have time right now.

lige om lidt.explanation: "Lige om lidt" means "in just a moment" and promises that something happens very soon: Maden er klar lige om lidt (The food is ready in just a moment).

forms.en: I am coming in just a moment.
We are leaving in just a moment.

sentence.da: Maden er klar **lige om lidt**.
sentence.en: The food will be ready in just a moment.

ligeglad.explanation: "Ligeglad" means "indifferent" and describes someone who does not care: Jeg er ligeglad (I do not mind). Said about a person it can sound rude: Han er ligeglad med andre (He does not care about others).

sentence.da: Jeg er **ligeglad**, om vi spiser pizza eller pasta.
sentence.en: I do not mind whether we eat pizza or pasta.

ligegyldig.explanation: "Ligegyldig" means "indifferent" or "unimportant". For a person, it means not caring: Hun virker ligegyldig (She seems indifferent). For a thing, it does not matter: Det er ligegyldigt (It is unimportant).

sentence.da: Han var **ligegyldig** og hørte ikke efter.
sentence.en: He was indifferent and did not listen.

ligesom.explanation: "Ligesom" means "just like". It is built from lige (just) and som (like). Use it to compare: Hun er ligesom sin mor (She is just like her mother).

forms.en: He is just like his father.

sentence.da: Du er **ligesom** din far.
sentence.en: You are just like your father.

lignende.explanation: "Lignende" means "similar" and comes before the word it describes: et lignende problem (a similar problem). To say one thing looks like another, use ligner: Han ligner sin far (He looks like his father).

sentence.da: Jeg har haft et **lignende** problem før.
sentence.en: I have had a similar problem before.

lilla.explanation: "Lilla" means "purple". Min taske er lilla means "My bag is purple". Do not mix it up with lyserød (pink).

sentence.da: Min nye taske er **lilla**.
sentence.en: My new bag is purple.

lille.explanation: "Lille" means "small" or "little", and it is also used for children. Compare en lille dreng (a little boy) with en stor dreng (a big boy).

sentence.da: Musen er meget **lille**.
sentence.en: The mouse is very small.

lim.explanation: "Lim" means "glue": Jeg bruger lim til papir (I use glue for paper). Vi bruger lim, ikke tape (We use glue, not tape).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge **lim**, så papiret sidder fast.
sentence.en: I need glue so the paper stays on.

linser.explanation: "Linser" means "lentils", small round seeds cooked in soups and stews: Vi spiser linser til middag (We eat lentils for dinner). One lentil is en linse, which also means a lens, as in en kontaktlinse (a contact lens).

sentence.da: Jeg laver suppe af røde **linser** og gulerødder.
sentence.en: I make soup from red lentils and carrots.

logisk.explanation: "Logisk" means "logical" and describes something that makes sense step by step: Det er logisk, at han er træt (It is logical that he is tired). Det er ikke logisk (That does not make sense).

sentence.da: Det er **logisk**, for to plus to er fire.
sentence.en: It is logical, because two plus two is four.

lokal.explanation: "Lokal" means "local", for things from the nearby area: en lokal avis (a local newspaper). Lokale nyheder (local news) is about your own town.

sentence.da: Jeg køber mad hos en **lokal** bager.
sentence.en: I buy food from a local baker.

lommepenge.explanation: "Lommepenge" means "pocket money", money children get to spend: Får du lommepenge? (Do you get pocket money?) It is built from en lomme (a pocket) and penge (money).

sentence.da: Min datter får hundrede kroner i **lommepenge**.
sentence.en: My daughter gets a hundred kroner in pocket money.

lotto.explanation: "Lotto" means "lotto", a game where you pick numbers and hope they match the draw: Vi spiller lotto hver lørdag (We play lotto every Saturday).

sentence.da: Han håber at vinde i **lotto** i weekenden.
sentence.en: He hopes to win at lotto this weekend.

lovlig.explanation: "Lovlig" means "legal", allowed by the law: Det er lovligt at cykle her (It is legal to bike here). Its opposite is ulovlig (illegal).

sentence.da: Det var en **lovlig** parkering, så han fik ingen bøde.
sentence.en: It was legal parking, so he got no fine.

luft.explanation: "Luft" means "air". I luften means "in the air". It is also the first part of en lufthavn (an airport), literally an air harbor.

sentence.da: Vi åbner vinduet for frisk **luft**.
sentence.en: We open the window for fresh air.

lukket.explanation: "Lukket" means "closed", for doors, shops, windows and roads. Butikken er lukket i dag means "The shop is closed today".

sentence.da: Butikken er **lukket** i dag.
sentence.en: The shop is closed today.

luksus.explanation: "Luksus" means "luxury", something very comfortable that you do not really need: Et langt bad er luksus (A long bath is a luxury). Det er luksus at have fri (It is a luxury to have time off).

sentence.da: Det er **luksus** at sove længe i weekenden.
sentence.en: It is a luxury to sleep in on the weekend.

lykke.explanation: "Lykke" means "happiness" and also "luck": Penge giver ikke lykke (Money does not bring happiness). Held og lykke! (Good luck!) is a common wish.

sentence.da: Jeg ønsker dig al **lykke** i dit nye hjem.
sentence.en: I wish you all happiness in your new home.

lykkelig.explanation: "Lykkelig" means "happy", in a deeper and longer-lasting way than glad (cheerful): Jeg er lykkelig med mit liv (I am happy with my life). For a good mood today, glad is more common: Jeg er glad i dag (I am happy today).

sentence.da: Hun er **lykkelig** med sit nye job.
sentence.en: She is happy with her new job.

lyn.explanation: "Et lyn" means "lightning", or "a flash of lightning": Et lyn slog ned i huset (Lightning struck the house). Hurtig som et lyn means "fast as lightning".

sentence.da: Et **lyn** slog ned i træet.
sentence.en: Lightning struck the tree.

lys.explanation: "Lys" means "light" (not dark) or "bright", for light colors and for rooms or days full of daylight. There is also a different word et lys, which means "a candle" or "a light".

sentence.da: Stuen er meget **lys** i dag.
sentence.en: The living room is very bright today.

lyseblå.explanation: "Lyseblå" means "light blue". It is lys (light) and blå (blue) joined into one word.

sentence.da: Himlen er **lyseblå** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is light blue today.

lysegrøn.explanation: "Lysegrøn" means "light green". It is lys (light) and grøn (green) joined into one word.

sentence.da: Salaten er **lysegrøn**.
sentence.en: The lettuce is light green.

lyserød.explanation: "Lyserød" means "pink". It is lys (light) and rød (red) joined into one word, so it is literally light red.

sentence.da: Grisen er **lyserød**.
sentence.en: The pig is pink.

læder.explanation: "Læder" means "leather": Skoene er lavet af læder (The shoes are made of leather). For fake leather, say kunstlæder (faux leather).

sentence.da: Min nye taske er lavet af **læder**.
sentence.en: My new bag is made of leather.

lækker.explanation: "Lækker" means "delicious" or "tasty", and also "great-looking": en lækker bil (a great-looking car).

sentence.da: Kagen er meget **lækker**.
sentence.en: The cake is really delicious.

længe.explanation: "Længe" means "for a long time": Jeg har ventet længe (I have waited a long time). For længe siden means "a long time ago". Do not mix it up with lang (long), which says how long something is: en lang vej (a long road).

sentence.da: Jeg har ventet **længe** på bussen.
sentence.en: I have waited a long time for the bus.

længst.explanation: "Længst" means "longest" for distance and time: Hvem har boet her længst? (Who has lived here the longest?) It also fits "furthest": Hvem bor længst væk? (Who lives the furthest away?)

sentence.da: Min bror bor **længst** fra os.
sentence.en: My brother lives the furthest from us.

lørdag.explanation: "En lørdag" means "a Saturday". På lørdag means "on Saturday" (the coming one), and "om lørdagen" means "on Saturdays" (every Saturday). Day names start with a small letter in Danish.

sentence.da: Vi har fri på **lørdag**.
sentence.en: We are off on Saturday.

løs.explanation: "Løs" means "loose", not fastened: Hunden er løs (The dog is loose). It also fits a knot: Knuden er løs (The knot is loose).

sentence.da: Min tand er **løs**, og den falder snart ud.
sentence.en: My tooth is loose, and it will fall out soon.
